title: Galois action on irreducible components of a locally finite type scheme: continuity, finiteness of the defining extension, and orbits
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over k, the three-part lemma states that the action of the opposite absolute Galois group on the irreducible components of X over the separable closure is continuous for the discrete topology, that every such component is defined over a finite extension of k, and that for an irreducible component T of X the base change T over the closure is a finite union of components lying in one Galois orbit (statement lines 1788-1809). The proof is uniform: given a component of the base change, pick an affine open U meeting it, write U = Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra, and observe that the prime ideal cutting out the component is generated by finitely many elements of A tensor the closure, which therefore already lie in A_{k'} for a finite subextension k', so the stabilizer of the component contains an open subgroup; this gives (1) and (2) (proof lines 1811-1831). Part (3) then takes a component of the base change mapping to T, uses finiteness of its orbit, and applies the descent result for Galois invariant closed subsets to the union of the orbit (proof lines 1833-1844). The claim is H2: one finiteness observation reused three times plus a descent step, with no step left to the reader.
